In my own game, I have a Fire-elemental enemy ability called "Ashen Plume" that inflicts a "damage over time" status effect, however, the status effect it inflicts is Poison.
Basically, the idea of the attack is that the enemy releases a cloud of toxic volcanic ash that damages the player's party with Fire/Poison-elemental physical damage & inflicts Poison status as well.
I also have a similar thing with the enemy ability "Soil Contamination", which deals Earth/Poison-elemental magical damage and also inflicts Poison status.
As for other Fire-elemental attacks that inflict status ailments:
"Incinerate" deals Fire-elemental magical damage & lowers the target's Defense by 50%.
"Scald" deals Fire/Water-elemental physical damage & lowers the target's Defense by 50%.
"Infernal Baptism" deals Fire-elemental magical damage & removes all positive status effects.
"Will-o'-the-Wisp" deals Fire-elemental magical damage & inflicts Curse status, which prevents the affected character from receiving Experience Points at the end of the battle.
"Sirocco" deals Fire/Wind-elemental magical damage & reduces the target's resistance to Fire-elemental damage by 50%.

So in my game, I have a few "Fire" skills that grant buffs or debuffs.

Click to expand...
Umm, not RPG Maker, Unreal Engine
.
In the past I mostly just played around with the various different versions of RPG Maker, never really making anything even remotely resembling a proper game.
I did at one point think about making a full game in RPG Maker MV that was separate from the RPG I had been working on since I was about 11 years old.  I made a full story outline detailing dungeons, bosses, etc. that was easily the length of an actual JRPG like Final Fantasy.  I even made a complete soundtrack for the game using a combination of RTP songs and free music found online.
The problem however was that I was developing this project while I was at same time starting to learn 3D modelling and programming to make a side-scrolling platform game based on a character and his entire world that my brother & I made when we were kids. Work on the RPG Maker project cut into my time working on my other project and eventually I decided that I couldn't work on both projects at once on top of the aforementioned other RPG I was developing.
Ultimately, it just made sense to me to stop working on the RPG Maker project and that my longtime dream RPG would be made in Unreal Engine as its the game engine I was already familiarizing myself with for the aforementioned side-scrolling platform game.
Its a shame because I quite liked the story, world & characters I created in the story outline.  Oh well, I've thought about reimagining the project into a potential sequel to my dream RPG if it ends up being a success but that's way, way done my list of priorities right now.
If you're wondering why I continue to hang out on a forum for a game engine that I'm not actually developing anything for, especially since I haven't been able to access my copy of RPG Maker MV for years, its just because I like following conversations about making RPGs.  I find talk about RPG game mechanics & story elements to be interesting and that's not something you can find on Unreal Engine's official forums.

posts.author: RachelTheSeeker
posts.body:
Question: how invested are you in the concept of "fire"? Just literally so? Or something more?
If this is mainly an attack, it's easy to make it deal damage over time. But there's plenty of symbolism to fire that can be applied. The fire itself may be literal, or not. Some common symbolism includes passion, anger, light, purification, destruction. I like the idea of fire as a balancing act -- something to be respected, feared for its danger yet beloved for the good it can do when controlled.
As someone who likes fire magic specialists in games, here's a few suggestions, some of which were taken from other games (Dark Souls' pyromancies are really cool, for instance).
If we're talking only RPG Maker 2003, there's definitely limits on what can be done from the ideas below. But most of these seem possible with VX Ace and onward, at the least, with or without scripts or plugins.
Blinding effect / lowers attack accuracy -- "pyrotechnics", "fireworks"
Berserk / attack enemies randomly with normal attacks -- "fiery rage", "moth to the flame", "hothead"
Causes damage to opponent when character is hit -- "boiling blood", "blazing barrier"
Stat buff, but take damage over time -- "power within", "kundalini liberation", "pants on fire"
Stat buff for free -- "galvanize", "flare up", "burning passion"
Healing, whether oneself or an ally -- "cauterize", "living flame"
Reviving KO'd allies -- "enkindle", "phoenix song", "from the ashes"
Remove buffs on enemy -- "burn away", "meltdown"
Instant death attack -- "incinerate", "immolate", "lava surge"
Lowers enemy stats -- "overheat", "fever", "scald"
Reduce incoming fire (or cold, water, etc) damage -- "heat barrier", "flash sweat", "warmth"
Remove status ailments from self -- "cleansing fever", "shed slag", "sudden sauna"
And of course, single-target fire attacks -- "blaze", "ignite", "fire bolt"
...and multi-target attacks -- "scorch", "brushfire", "fireball", "fire wall"
...and causing damage over time -- "singe", "will o' wisp", "brush burn"
...and even more physical attacks instead of magical -- "flame blade", "molotov cocktail", "dragon's breath"
...and even some sci-fi attacks -- "pyrokinesis", "plasma rifle (in the 40-watt range)", "mitochondrial revolt"
As you can see, fire is a pretty versatile element with a little thought toward its uses and symbolism. But to be fair, I may just be an armchair pyro, for all I know. Make of it what you will.

posts.author: Tech
posts.body:
So many states you can do with fire spells!
Weld-Increase defenses (like, welded-on hillbilly scrap-armor to an ally's existing outfit)
Enchant Weapon-add bonus fire-element attack power
Flashbang-stun/blind
Burning-wildly fluctuating DOT
Cauterize-healing
Candle-resistance to darkness-aligned spells/debuffs
Cozy-resistance to ice/water-aligned spells/debuffs
Fireball/grenade/etc-direct elemental attacks
Heat Metal-reduced attack/defense (their armor and/or weapons are now merrily glowing red)
Cooking-bonus to the next healing item used
Smoke-poison and/or blinding; maybe with a Silence effect to represent coughing.

posts.author: Monad
posts.body:
Personally I would think about how I want my battle system balanced before I start stylizing them as fire/water/metal etc. I mean if your game has fictional magic you can write a fictional explanation for any effect it does.
I thought it was cool in Valkyria Revolution that some AoE element attacks would also give party members in the AoE the corresponding stat boost to the element (can’t remember offhand but I think fire gave atk boost) don’t know if in Rm2k3 you could give a boost to the user and damage target at the same time though.
In Tales of Zestiria the elements were correlated with other stats and ailments, like fire was mag atk buff/debuff and burn, and having any debuff would make it more likely to get hit with an ailment, and getting any ailment would block healing. So they’re was a mix of element specific effects (debuff/ailment) and universal effects (healing block)
Another idea is that it doesn’t have to have a state effect either, you could have some elements that do states and some that are unique for their balance, like fire could just be a cheap/weak attack skill to use.
